transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. It's probably just a silly little thing, but... well, what brings me in is that I just can’t seem to turn off the worrying once it starts. 

I try to be very organized, and even when I tell myself I’ve made the lists, and I've checked all the dates, and done absolutely all I reasonably can... my mind just keeps going. It's a bit embarrassing to admit at my age, really, because I know I shouldn't fret so much. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it properly for you.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different things, not just one specific issue, and does it feel difficult to control that worry even when you try?

Yes, exactly. I, um... I hope I don't sound too dramatic saying this, because I know people have much bigger problems, but yes, it’s quite a few different things. 

My mind just keeps roaming. It'll jump from the exhibition schedule I'm helping out with, to my daughter's travel plans, and then suddenly I'm agonizing over whether the house gutters need fixing. I know they're just normal, everyday things, and I really shouldn't complain. But sometimes... well, these small things start to feel as if they could just unravel into something much bigger. 

I try my absolute best to rein it in and be sensible about it, I really do. Is that... does that answer your question, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, or muscle tension, when you're worrying like this?

Well, I... I suppose I do get a little fidgety sometimes. I don't want to make it sound like I'm pacing the floors all night or anything extreme like that! It's just... sometimes when I'm sitting in my own living room, trying to relax, I feel a bit wound up. 

I'll notice I'm tapping my fingers on the armrest while I'm on the phone, or I'll suddenly feel the need to get up and straighten a picture frame or adjust a cushion. It's almost like sitting perfectly still just makes me feel a tiny bit jumpy. It's probably just a silly habit I've picked up, really. I hope that's the sort of thing you were asking about? I don't want to waste your time with unimportant details.
Do you often feel unusually tired or low on energy, even if you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Well, I... I suppose I do get a bit tired, yes. But honestly, at my age, I think it's probably just normal to slow down a little bit, isn't it? I don't want to make a fuss over nothing. 

But, um, I have noticed that even when I sleep through the whole night, I'll wake up feeling... well, almost as if I've already put in half a day's work before I've even gotten out of bed. And by the time I've just done a few little things around the house—like watering the garden beds or just sorting out some papers for my book club—I find I really need to just sit down for a moment and gather myself. 

It's nothing terrible, really, just a bit of tiredness. I just try to push through it and not complain. Is that... is that helpful for you to know, Doctor? I hope I'm not overstating it.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or keeping your attention on tasks, like reading or following a conversation, because your mind is preoccupied with worries?

Oh, well... no, I don't think so. I mean, I can still read my books just fine, and I certainly don't want you to think I'm losing my marbles or anything! I try very hard to be a good listener when my friends are talking. 

Sometimes, if I'm being completely honest, my mind might wander just a tiny bit if I'm trying to read a very dense article, or... or if someone is telling a very long story. But I think everyone does that, don't they? It's just a normal part of getting older, I'm sure. I always make sure to nod and smile so no one feels ignored. I haven't really noticed any real trouble focusing, though. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm answering this correctly for you.
Do you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or do you wake up too early and find it hard to get back to sleep?

Well, I... I suppose my sleep isn't always absolutely perfect, but really, who sleeps like a baby at my age? I certainly don't want to complain about a few restless nights here and there. 

Sometimes it takes me a little while to drift off, maybe because I'm just going over my to-do list for the next day, making sure I haven't forgotten anything important for the house. And occasionally I might wake up a bit early, but I just use that time to quietly plan out my morning so I don't disturb anyone. I really don't think it's anything out of the ordinary, though. I'm usually able to get enough rest to keep going. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I'd hate to make a mountain out of a molehill if it's just normal aging.
Do you ever find yourself especially anxious or self-conscious in social situations, or worry a lot about how you're being perceived by others?

Oh, heavens, no. I mean... I wouldn't say I'm especially anxious or anything like that. I've always enjoyed being around people, really. I go to my book club, and I see my neighbors, and we always have a lovely time. 

I suppose... well, I do like to make sure I'm dressed appropriately and that I'm not saying anything foolish, but I think that's just good manners, isn't it? Nobody wants to be the person who talks too much or makes a faux pas. Sometimes I might replay a conversation in my head afterwards, just to make sure I didn't accidentally offend anyone, but... but I'm sure everyone does that to some extent. I certainly don't let it ruin my day or keep me from going out. 

I try very hard to be polite and agreeable. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm overly worried about it, Doctor? I just like to be a good friend and neighbor, that's all. Does that answer your question alright?

Have you ever had sudden episodes where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came out of the blue and reached a peak within just a few minutes? Things like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you couldn't breathe?

Oh, my goodness, no. Nothing like that. That sounds quite frightening, actually! I've never had anything come on suddenly like that out of nowhere. 

I mean, if I'm rushing around the house trying to get ready for guests, my heart might beat a little faster, but that's just because I'm trying to be a good hostess and get everything done on time. I certainly wouldn't call it an episode or anything dramatic. I've never felt like I couldn't breathe or had intense fear... I'm a fairly calm person, really. I hope that's a good thing? I'd hate for you to think I'm holding anything back, but I really haven't experienced anything like what you're describing. I'm doing my best to give you the right answers, Doctor. Is that helpful?
Do you ever find yourself feeling irritable or easily frustrated, especially when you're caught up in these worries?

Oh, dear, I certainly hope not. I really pride myself on being patient and... well, agreeable with people. I'd hate to think I was ever snapping at anyone just because I had a lot on my mind. 

I mean, if I'm trying to get the house ready and time is running short, I suppose I might get a tiny bit flustered internally? But I always try to keep a smile on my face. I would never want to take anything out on my husband or my friends, or make them feel bad. It's just not polite to be irritable, is it? I really try my very best to be pleasant to be around, no matter what I'm thinking about. 

I hope that's alright, Doctor? I just don't think of myself as a frustrated or angry person at all.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any days where you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like your book club or time with family?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean... I still go to my book club every month, and I wouldn't miss Sunday dinners with the family for the world. I've always been a very cheerful person, really. 

I suppose there are days when I feel a little tired, but at my age, who doesn't? And I always make sure to push through and get everything done. I would never want to let anyone down by just... sitting around moping, you know? It's so important to keep busy and keep a positive attitude. 

I really do still enjoy all my little activities. I hope that's what you were looking for, Doctor? I try to be very upbeat, I really do.
Would you say that you have been feeling this way—being really worried about everyday things—nearly every day for at least the past several months?

Well, I suppose... yes, it has been a little while. Maybe about seven months or so? It started shortly after a dear friend of mine passed away. We had a few little projects we were involved in together, and I just stepped in to try and keep things moving, you know? Just trying to be helpful and do the right thing. 

So I've been quite focused on making sure all those everyday details are handled properly. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around wringing my hands and worrying all day—I just like to be thorough and responsible! It's perfectly natural to want to stay on top of things when you take on extra tasks, isn't it? 

I hope that answers your question, Doctor. I really am trying my best to explain it properly for you. Does that timeline make sense?
